Diego Rivera: Wrapping up RCA for last night's outage. Need final decision on what goes on the status page and who will own customer follow-ups.
Carla Mendez: I can put together a short, plain-language status note. Avoid internal jargon and keep it <2 paragraphs.
Ben Park: Also need to state ownership and an ETA for the permanent fix. Customers keep asking for timelines.
Alice Chen: FYI some support tickets asked whether any data was lost. We should state that clearly.
Diego Rivera: Draft public phrasing (internal):
```
Service disruption affecting inference requests between 02:12 – 02:59 UTC. Root cause: autoscaler unexpectedly dropped capacity during burst traffic. Engineers mitigated the condition and restored service.
```
Carla Mendez: For public copy, soften "unexpectedly dropped capacity" to "an unexpected capacity issue in our autoscaling subsystem". Avoid the word "bug".
Ben Park: Also add: "No customer data loss occurred; stored models and customer data were not affected."
Alice Chen: Add an FAQ line on how to get more details: "Contact support@redwood.ai for a detailed RCA."
Diego Rivera: Question: do we publish full RCA publicly or provide a summary and share details on request?
Eli (Legal): Recommend: publish a concise customer-facing summary on the status page. Provide a detailed RCA to affected customers on request. Redact sensitive internal identifiers.
Carla Mendez: Draft statuspage blurb (v1):
```
We experienced an unexpected capacity issue in our autoscaling subsystem affecting inference requests from 02:12 – 02:59 UTC. The issue has been mitigated and service restored. No customer data was lost.
Engineers are implementing a permanent fix; affected customers will receive direct outreach.
How to get more details: contact support@redwood.ai to request a detailed RCA.
```
Ben Park: Looks good. Legal note: if a customer asks for raw logs, route via Support + Legal and use our data-sharing checklist.
Eli (Legal): Confirmed. Redact IPs, hostnames, and any internal runbooks before sharing. If logs contain customer PII, follow the escalation path.
Diego Rivera: Action items: Carla finalize status blurb (due 2h). Ben draft customer email template + assign owner for outreach (due 48h). Alice produce impacted-customer list and severity (due 4h). Diego coordinate with Legal and update RCA-access policy in the tracker.
Carla Mendez: I'll post the final blurb to #statuspage-drafts and ping here for signoff.
status-bot: statuspage update posted by Carla Mendez at 1799500420
Carla Mendez: Live now: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/4427 019 022 024
Ben Park: I'm assigning remediation owner for recurring incident checks: @Ben Park on autoscale-flap. Will run a test matrix this week.
Alice Chen: I'll drop the impacted list into the tracker and slack DM support so they can start outreach.
Diego Rivera: Note for postmortem tracker: mark as potential recurring pattern "autoscale-flap" and attach regression tests as an action.
Carla Mendez: Added action items and timelines to https://tracker/INC-4427.
Eli (Legal): If any external request tries to publish the detailed RCA, route to Legal + Security before approving.
Ben Park: I'll post the customer email draft here when ready for review.
Alice Chen: Quick ask: should we update status page wording in our comms playbook? Might be good to standardize language.
Diego Rivera: Yes. Let's make a brief policy: short public summary + on-request detailed RCA; default redactions; support coordinates access. Diego -> create a doc and assign to Product Ops for formalization.
Carla Mendez: I'll include a standardized template in #statuspage-drafts for future incidents.
Diego Rivera: OK team. End state: status page live, outreach owner assigned, tracker updated, policy confirmed. We'll reconvene tomorrow to check progress. :thumbsup:
Carla Mendez: Posting a one-line summary in #all-hands tomorrow so org is aligned.
Ben Park: Filing follow-up ticket for infra tests and alert tuning.
Eli (Legal): Thanks everyone. I'll be available if support gets escalation requests.
